rationale: The candidate reads coherently across all four views as one stepped dominant mass, so gesture clarity and repair integrity are strong. The silhouette is legible and capacity-bearing enough to avoid a flat rejection, but the section is still mostly repetitive setbacks rather than a truly authored public section. The main failure is programmatic: the mass is a sealed, stacked object with very little visible active ground threshold or usable public void, while the brief requires an active street edge plus one clear court/terrace/entry void. The blue access edge is acknowledged only weakly, with no compelling carve, seam, or undercut directed to that frontage. It therefore feels closer to a generic stepped podium/object than a neighborhood living building with an active ground condition. References 1-3 support the need for courtyard/threshold/public edge logic; reference 4 is only partially relevant for a differentiated ground base; reference 5 is counterfactual and useful only as a reminder that long linear gestures are not the same as a bridge.
